name: Saints Philip and James
history: Two of the Twelve, honoured together since their relics were placed in the Church of the Holy Apostles in Rome. Philip of Bethsaida brought Nathanael to Jesus and asked Him at the Last Supper to show them the Father. James, son of Alphaeus, is identified in the Western tradition with James, the brother of the Lord and bishop of Jerusalem.
life: Saint John’s Gospel gives us Philip in a few sharp moments. Called by Jesus, he went at once to Nathanael: come and see. Before the feeding of the five thousand Jesus tested him by asking where to buy bread, and Philip could only count the cost. When some Greeks wished to see Jesus, they came to Philip. At the Last Supper he said, ‘Lord, show us the Father,’ and heard the answer: whoever has seen me has seen the Father. Tradition says he preached in Phrygia and died at Hierapolis. James, son of Alphaeus, is called James the Less. The Latin Church has long identified him with James the brother of the Lord, who led the Church in Jerusalem, spoke at the Council of Jerusalem and, according to Josephus, was stoned around 62. Their relics were enshrined in Rome in the sixth century.
prayerTo: Saints Philip and James, apostles of the Lord, you saw the face of the Father in Jesus and gave your lives for Him. Pray for the Church, for those who seek God, and for me, that I may see Christ more clearly, and that my faith may show itself in works. Amen.
penance: James wrote that faith without works is dead. Do one practical work of mercy today, and bring someone, as Philip did, to come and see.
meditation: Lord, show us the Father, and we shall be satisfied. Have I been so long with you, and yet you do not know me? Where have you missed Him?
